newsitem.title: USA: Clinton inauguration falls short in economic impact.
newsitem.headline: Clinton inauguration falls short in economic impact.

text.p: President Clinton's inauguration boosted the Washington area economy by about $70 million, falling short of expectations by about $25 million, a city organisation said Tuesday.
The Washington, D.C. Convention and Visitors Association estimated "the total economic impact for the Washington region from out-of-town visitors to the inaugural was $70 million."

That was based on a survey that showed average hotel occupancy of 79 percent over the four-day inaugural period and translated into an improvement in the economy about $25 million less than the $95 million that had been expected.

Four years ago, an estimated $110 million in business activity was generated by Clinton's first inaugural, a spokeswoman for the organisation said. Since second inaugurals traditionally generate less enthusiasm, the group last fall projected a smaller economic boost from the Jan. 20 inaugural.
